stem: A release engineer at Kestrel Bank sees that `terraform apply` printed nothing about locking and wants to know whether the shared state was protected from a colleague's simultaneous apply. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Locking happens only when `-lock=true` is added to the command line, so this particular apply ran with no protection from the colleague's run
Every backend locks state automatically, so the silence confirms that the state was protected
Locking covers `apply` but not state-modifying commands such as `terraform state mv`
If the backend supports locking, Terraform locks silently for any write operation; a backend without lock support gives no protection

rationale: Locking is automatic on all operations that could write state when the backend supports it, and Terraform prints nothing about it, so silence says nothing either way; if lock acquisition fails Terraform stops. Not every backend supports locking, which is why checking the backend's documentation matters. Requiring `-lock=true` is wrong because locking is on by default and only switched off with `-lock=false`. Limiting locking to apply is wrong because locking covers all operations that could write state.
